content:
- Overestimate prices after recent spikes; model tends to overshoot post-peak sentiment (e.g., +0.37 sentiment → forecast peaks too high).
- Underestimate downward trends when sentiment is negative and persistent (e.g., -0.43 sentiment → model fails to drop below 70).
- Lag in correction: model often delays downward adjustment by 2–3 days after negative sentiment spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects upward after strong negative sentiment, then fails to revert to mean.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts overestimate early in the window when sentiment is volatile; later days show underestimation if sentiment turns negative.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.2, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day; if sentiment < -0.3, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day to counteract bias.
